title: Circuit languages have polynomial advice algorithms
statement: Every language recognized by a family of Boolean circuits with fan-in at most two and size at most $a(n+1)^k$ on inputs of length $n$, for some natural numbers $a,k$, is decidable by a deterministic finite Turing machine given an advice string depending only on the input length. For some natural numbers $c,C,d$, the advice string for length $n$ has exactly $C(n+1)^d$ bits, and the machine decides the language on every input of length $n$ within $c(n^c+1)$ steps when given the input and advice in the stated pair encoding.
